Hill's personal release on the same bill, 2026-07-22, mentions credit unions zero times: 'it's our local banks that step up,' and he opens 'As a former community banker.' Not misconduct — he claimed nothing he did not deliver. Recorded because it independently confirms the bank_primary classification of H.R.6955 from the sponsor's own mouth.

Committee section-by-section verified 2026-07-29: 8 titles, 30+ sections, all bank-directed. Credit unions appear exactly twice, both as 'NCUA' inside a list of regulators. No substantive credit union provision. The claim of credit-union benefit is therefore hollow on the merits — which is what sustains this event at severity 2 even after the multiplier is reduced.

_multiplier_note: REVISED 2026-07-29 from 2.0 to 1.0, at PARITY with Barr's structurally identical MS-2026-003. The 2.0 was argued on the ground that Barr's was a personal release while this is the committee's institutional voice under Hill's gavel. That distinction is real but it does not survive the rest of the record: 'community banks and credit unions' is Hill's consistent register, not a one-off appropriation — he used the same phrasing in his floor statement on the same bill the same day — and he has a genuine, if thin, delivery record (he floor-managed H.R.975 Credit Union Board Modernization, H.R.4437 and H.R.4544 to passage; see delivery_ledger.ndjson). Pricing an identical instrument higher for him than for Barr was reverse-engineering toward a destination. 1.0 is the defensible value. What actually distinguishes the two members is now carried by the delivery ledger, where it belongs: Barr delivers 0.00, Hill delivers 3.00.
